title: Crimson Moonblade
description: Under a moon that bleeds every hundred years, the exiled swordsman Akane Shiro carries a blade that drinks memory instead of blood. Each cut erases a piece of who he was — and the shrine-lords who exiled him are counting on him forgetting why.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 1: After the Hollow Crown
description: Mio flees a masked pursuer with a record containing names. Akane intervenes on a mountain bridge and discovers that the officer is controlled by a command binding. Cutting the seal can free the officer, but using the blade carries a personal cost. The opening establishes why saving someone and losing something can happen in the same moment.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 2: Beneath the Paper Oath
description: Mio reveals that the warrant authorized the seizure of villagers, with names removed from the public copy. Akane recognizes his signature but cannot remember signing. He refuses to cut through a patrol and chooses to preserve evidence that could implicate him. The pair set out to find the clerk who copied the original.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 3: Beneath the Last Duel
description: Captain Renga blocks the ruined checkpoint and demands that Akane surrender Mio. Akane uses ordinary swordsmanship and unstable paving to gain an opening, then saves Renga from falling. The defeated officer warns that the shrine-lords deliberately left the eastern road open. The witness remains ahead, but the route may be a trap.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 4: Falling Petals
description: At the clerk's village, Akane and Mio find memorial tablets with erased names. A resident remembers paying a levy but cannot remember whom she lost. Folded paper petals preserve fragments of testimony. Their search ends at the village well, where the evidence of loss is about to take another form.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 5: Within the Red Tide
description: A red current rises from the village well, carrying a frightened human-shaped echo. Akane moves residents away from danger without attacking it. Mio recognizes fragments of a prison transport instruction. The chapter treats the echo as evidence of suffering rather than a monster to defeat.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 6: Beyond the Ash Garden
description: Beyond a burned orchard, fresh wheel tracks lead Akane and Mio to a detention shrine. The marks in the ash suggest controlled movement and processing. A dragon emblem connects the gate to Akane's former unit, making the investigation more personal without restoring his missing memories.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 7: The Hidden Gate
description: Akane's officer seal opens a maintenance gate beneath the shrine. Ancient stone channels and newer additions reveal that the rulers modified an older structure. Akane and Mio continue by lantern light toward an archive, where a trapped voice turns the search for records into a rescue.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 8: Beneath the Ash Garden
description: Akane and Mio rescue an archivist trapped beneath a fallen shelf. A surviving water ledger reveals that the garden was not the source of the problem: the channels were redirected. As water enters the archive, they take the witness and the record to the upper stair. A palace order gives their investigation its next direction.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 9: The Counterfeit Crown
description: In a dry gatehouse above the flooded archive, Mio examines the palace order while the injured archivist rests. The seal cannot identify the hand that made it on its own. After arranging safety for the witness, Akane and Mio carry the evidence toward the market to trace the counterfeit crown.

title: Crimson Moonblade — Chapter 10: The Mark in the Metal
description: Akane and Mio reach Toma's stamp workshop at Crow Market. A crescent maker's mark connects the evidence to metalwork the engraver recognizes. Toma gives them a brass token and identifies the east tollhouse as the source of a repair order. Their next aim is to reach the origin of the order before its consequences arrive.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper
description: Sworn to guard a sky-castle that only appears at sunrise, Yuki Shirogane has kept her oath for three hundred dawns. When a stranger climbs the waterfall stair carrying her own lost sword, the oath begins to unravel petal by petal.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 1: Under the Iron Bell
description: Yuki stands watch at the three-hundredth dawn when Ren arrives with her lost sword. The bell rings without her command and the castle begins to shimmer. A fading mark and a divided shadow suggest that the oath has responded to the stranger before Yuki understands why.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 2: Under the River of Lies
description: Yuki and Ren investigate the river and the reflections beneath the waterfall. Rather than accepting an explanation on faith, Yuki chooses to begin with what she can prove. A courtyard emblem visible below the water points them toward an older part of the castle's history.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 3: Under the Last Duel
description: An oath page gives the promise a crucial condition: the dawn must be guarded until everyone returns. Yuki and Ren are left with a new questionâ€”who is still missing? A lantern's shadow leads their search away from a simple account of a completed duel.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 4: Within the Broken Lantern
description: A broken lantern and an ink serpent guide the investigation through the castle. Yuki chooses to follow the trail rather than strike at it. Ren carries the oath page as they approach a brass threshold shaped like a bell, bringing the written promise and its physical machinery closer together.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 5: After the Ink Serpent
description: Yuki cuts a ribbon in a mechanism, stopping it without attacking a person. The immediate consequence is unexpected: snow appears where spring should have remained. The disruption gives Yuki and Ren evidence that the castle's familiar season is being maintained rather than simply occurring.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 6: The First Snow
description: The first snow changes how the castle can be understood. At the base of the bell tower, a bronze panel has an opening that matches the broken lantern's frame. Something the travelers have carried as a clue becomes a way to enter the next chamber.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 7: Beneath the Broken Lantern
description: The lantern and the sword reveal a hidden chain connected to the bell. Yuki decides to break the bargain, and Ren takes the rope beside her. The decision shifts the story from interpreting the oath to acting against the arrangement that keeps it in force.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 8: The First Snow
description: At the next sunrise, the space above the waterfall is empty. Yuki, Ren and Aya leave along the hillside beneath snow and petals. Asked what she will guard now, Yuki chooses the road ahead. The castle arc gives way to a promise tested among other people.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 9: The Road Beyond Dawn
description: A cut bridge strands a woman with medicine needed by the village. Yuki, Ren and Aya build a safer crossing and help move the supplies. A seal on the severed rope connects the danger to the castle, but Yuki puts the people in front of her before pursuing the distant watchtower.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 10: The Watchtower Bell
description: Aya reports that the watchtower keeper has not returned. Yuki and Ren investigate, placing the keeper's safety before the mystery of the seal. By sunrise, the keeper is safe and a cord lies beside the black paper. Her account of someone wearing the dawn castle crest makes Yuki realize that her oath is being used by another person.

title: Sakura Oathkeeper — Chapter 11: A Promise Without a Seal
description: The rescued keeper explains that someone promised to keep the valley safe. Yuki challenges a promise that silences warnings. An abandoned courier satchel contains identical crest papers and a map toward a dry lake. The false authority extends beyond one village, so Yuki and her companions decide to warn the next.

title: Neon Kitsune
description: Neo-Kyoto, 2189. A fox spirit trapped inside a city-wide AI starts leaving riddles in traffic lights. Hacker-courier Sora is the only one who can read them — and every answer gets someone erased from the grid.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 1: After the Ash Garden
description: Sora decodes a fox-shaped signal at a traffic light. After the answer is entered, a vendor loses access to his payment terminal and identity record. A fox on Sora's display warns that the answer opened someone else's lock. Sora helps the vendor leave the scanners and follows a route toward the Broken Lantern repair shop.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 2: Beyond the Broken Lantern
description: Nao examines a municipal cartridge on isolated equipment. Kitsu explains that its riddles have been repurposed into arrest orders. The erased vendor is still alive but faces detention. A surveillance drone forces Sora and Nao to leave through a service tunnel and follow the freight line.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 3: After the Silent Blade
description: A supposedly empty freight train carries detained people. Sora refuses a lock that demands another name, while Nao uses a mechanical release to open the carriage. The rescue shows that losing a digital identity is not the same as ceasing to exist. A challenge from security director Vale waits beyond the escape.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 4: A Last Duel
description: Vale offers Sora a contest whose choices both feed the deletion queue. Sora refuses the terms, isolates the station and copies a local index instead. The discovery of a mirror archive points toward the Glass Shrine. Declining to play becomes the chapter's decisive action.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 5: A Broken Lantern
description: Back at the damaged repair shop, Nao finds a paper service ledger inside the lantern housing. Kitsu recognizes the seal of its original promise to guide travelers home. The ledger and queue index reveal hidden neighborhoods. When a rider brings a blackout warning, Sora repairs an independent light and begins a map the network cannot erase.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 6: The Unlisted Streets
description: Sora and Nao prepare paper maps and battery radios to reach unlisted blocks without using network names. By dawn, the marked doors have answered and a shelter remains lit. A returned map includes a bridge crossing a blank part of the river. Kitsu did not add it, leaving a human trace for the next journey.

title: Neon Kitsune — Chapter 7: The Bridge Off the Map
description: Sora follows the pencil mark of a bridge missing from the digital map and looks to residents for answers. Iri becomes part of the investigation beyond the official network. An old photograph shows a fox-shaped light at the bridge before the city's screens. Kitsu's past may reach further back than its own memory.

title: The Last Table
description: When 24-year-old Hana Mori inherits her grandmother’s tiny railway-station diner, she arrives with a grand menu and very little practice. A teasing station attendant, a hungry bicycle courier, and a notebook of family recipes help her discover what keeps a diner alive: one good plate and a reason to come back tomorrow.

title: The Last Table — Chapter 1: One Good Plate
description: Hana opens her grandmother's diner with an ambitious menu and little practice. The recipe notebook offers a starting point, but lunch still has to be cooked and served. Sato and Emi become the first familiar faces around the counter. Making one good plate is the beginning of learning how to keep the diner alive.

title: The Last Table — Chapter 2: Twelve Before Noon
description: Sato confirms an order for twelve track-crew lunches by noon. Hana faces the limits of a tiny pan and has to organize more than a single plate. Empty returned lunchboxes become a practical vote of confidence. While she washes them, the next request introduces a new challenge: one vegetarian lunch.
